item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-20 23:59
Institution: Univ. PARMA, Parma
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/MVET-01 Anatomia e fisiologia veterinaria

This project aims to characterize the anatomical and molecular changes occurring in stem cell niches by integrating advanced spatial profiling technologies with histological and molecular analyses, in order to identify the anatomical and molecular determinants underlying the age-related decline in regenerative function. The objective is to define how the structural and functional organization of stem cell niches is remodeled during aging and to identify spatial molecular signatures associated with pro-regenerative or pro-senescent states. item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Characterization of the transmission dynamics of Xylella fastidiosa by insect vectors in vineyards and semi-natural environments (Univ. BARI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-20 23:55
Institution: Univ. BARI, Lussemburgo
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-05 Patologia vegetale ed entomologia

*Xylella fastidiosa* subsp. *fastidiosa* Sequence Type 1 (Xff-ST1) represents a new threat to European viticulture, particularly in light of its detection in table grape vineyards in Apulia. The project aims to understand the epidemiology of *Xylella fastidiosa* in table grape vineyards and to investigate the role of spontaneous vegetation and non-cultivated environments in supporting insect vector populations and acting as sources or recipients of the bacterium. The results will improve the understanding of vector-pathogen-host interactions, identify key epidemiological risk factors, and provide data useful for risk assessment and the development of effective disease management strategies.

The project involves the development and validation of innovative agronomic protocols for the valorization of durum wheat. The strategies adopted will include the use of new generation biostimulants (both microbial and non-microbial), with the aim of reducing chemical inputs and promoting environmental sustainability. The effectiveness of these approaches will be evaluated in the field through the monitoring of the physiological and production parameters of the crop.
